steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar to open the sidebar.
Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type a short plain sentence, for example: Explain this file in one line.
Click the send button at the bottom right of the composer (tooltip "Send (Enter)") or press Enter.
Look: the message appears in the chat as your message, the box clears, and a reply starts.
S13.01.where: AGI Code sidebar (activity bar) > composer box with placeholder "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) button

S13.02.note: Line breaks are kept by the native text box; the code does not rewrite them on send, but I did not trace the send payload to confirm the kept breaks reach the reply.
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type a first line, press Shift+Enter, type a second line, press Shift+Enter, type a third line.
Look: the cursor moves to a new line each time and nothing is sent.
Press Enter to send, then look at the sent message in the chat and check the line breaks are still there.
S13.02.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…"

S13.03.note: The growth is a layout rule in autoResize (height capped at 140px); the cap is in code, not a visible setting.
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type or paste many lines (press Shift+Enter between them) without sending.
Look: the box gets taller with each line until it reaches about 140 px, then stops growing and a scroll bar appears inside it.
S13.03.where: Composer box "Describe a task…" grows as text is added

S13.06.note: The button is disabled when the box is empty, when the runtime is blocked, or while a new thread is being set up; no visible reason text is shown next to it, only the tooltip changes, so the disabled reason may not be visible.
steps: With the composer empty, look at the send button: it is greyed out and cannot be clicked.
Type a message in the box "Describe a task…".
Look: the send button becomes active.
Click the send button and look for the message in the chat.
S13.06.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer > send button at the bottom right (tooltip "Send (Enter)")

S13.07.needs: a reply that takes a few seconds to generate
S13.07.note: Escape also stops a reply, but only when the setting Escape stops response is turned on (it is off by default).
steps: Send a prompt that gives a long answer, for example: List 30 facts about the Moon.
While the reply is still streaming, look at the bottom of the composer for the stop button (tooltip "Stop response").
Click "Stop response".
Look: the reply stops, the text already written stays in the chat, and the send controls return.
S13.07.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer, while a reply is generating > Stop response button

S13.09.note: The Send key setting can change which key sends; with it set to Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter behaves differently.
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…" and type some text.
Press Shift+Enter.
Look: a new line is added and the message is not sent.
Optional: open Settings > Send key and check the option text matches the behaviour seen.
S13.09.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > Shift+Enter (default). Setting: Settings > Session behavior > Send key

S13.10.note: The composer is a plain text box and the code adds no undo handler of its own; undo comes from the browser text box. I did not find a line of code that blocks it.
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…" and type a word.
Type a second word, then press Cmd+Z.
Look: the last typed text is taken back.
Press Shift+Cmd+Z and look: the text comes back.
S13.10.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > Cmd+Z and Shift+Cmd+Z

S13.11.needs: a file or an image on the clipboard
steps: Copy a text snippet and an image or a file from Finder.
Click in the box "Describe a task…" and press Cmd+V with the text.
Look: the text appears in the box.
Press Cmd+V with the image or file, and look for a chip in the strip above the box (Pending attachments).
S13.11.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > paste (Cmd+V)

S13.12.needs: a web page or document with formatted text
S13.12.note: The paste handler only takes over file pastes; formatted text relies on the native plain-text box, not on a code path that strips markup.
steps: Copy a formatted line from a web page (bold or coloured text, links).
Click in the box "Describe a task…" and press Cmd+V.
Look: only plain text appears, with no bold, colours or links.
S13.12.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > paste (Cmd+V) formatted text

S13.15.note: The counter is filled from a context message after a turn; I did not confirm when it first appears before any turn.
steps: Send a short message and wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the bottom row of the composer, next to the model button, for a small token count.
Hover over the count and read the tooltip.
S13.15.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer bottom row, small counter beside the Auto model button, shown after a turn finishes

S13.20.needs: a skill available to the account for the sidebar rows; the VS Code Chat view for the follow-up buttons
S13.20.note: The follow-up buttons exist only in VS Code's native Chat view, not in the AGI Code sidebar; the sidebar offers Skills, Projects and Connected apps rows instead of follow-up questions.
steps: Open a new chat so the start screen is showing.
Look for the group heading "Skills" under the start screen.
Click one skill row: the composer fills with a prompt for that skill.
Optional: in the VS Code Chat view, ask a question to the AGI Code participant and look for follow-up buttons under the answer.
S13.20.where: AGI Code sidebar > empty chat (start screen) > Skills rows. Also VS Code Chat view > @agi answer > follow-up buttons

S13.21.needs: a saved prompt command in your account or CLI (not confirmed which exist)
S13.21.note: The code puts the command name in the composer for prompt-type commands (source prompt); whether the user's own saved templates appear depends on the runtime list, which I did not check.
steps: Click the "Commands" button next to the + button in the composer.
Look for a command listed from your prompt commands and click it.
Look: the composer shows the command name with a space after it, ready for your own text.
Type your text after it and press Enter.
S13.21.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer > Commands button (/) > pick a prompt command

S13.22.note: If no command matches, the list shows "No matching command"; the list loads once commands arrive.
steps: Click in the box "Describe a task…" and type a single slash /.
Look: a list of commands opens above the box.
Type a letter after the slash, for example /co, and look: the list narrows to matching commands.
Use the arrow keys and Enter, or click a row, to choose one.
S13.22.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > type /

S13.23.needs: a skill listed under Skills on the start screen
S13.23.note: The composer fills with a sentence asking to use the skill; no skill chip is shown in the composer, and a check that the next message runs with it depends on the reply.
steps: Open a new chat so the start screen shows.
Under the heading "Skills", click one skill row.
Look: the composer is filled with a sentence naming that skill, with the cursor at the end.
Type what you want done and send it, then check the reply uses that skill.
S13.23.where: AGI Code sidebar > empty chat (start screen) > Skills > click a skill

S13.24.needs: a VS Code build with the Chat view
S13.24.note: The sidebar composer has no agent picker; the mention exists only in VS Code's native Chat, and the code skips it if the Chat API is missing.
steps: Open the VS Code Chat view.
Type @ in its input box and look for the AGI Code entry.
Select AGI Code and send a question.
Look: the reply comes from AGI Code.
S13.24.where: VS Code Chat view (the native chat, not the AGI Code sidebar) > type @ > AGI Code

S13.26.needs: a workspace folder open in VS Code
S13.26.note: The code inserts an @path token; I did not trace that the file contents are added to the message.
steps: Click in the box "Describe a task…" and type @.
Type part of a file name, for example @app.
Look: a list titled Workspace files and symbols opens above the box.
Choose a file with the arrow keys and Enter, or click it, then look for the @ file token in the box and send.
S13.26.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > type @ then part of a file name

S13.31.needs: an open editor or a selection in VS Code for some items
S13.31.note: Project chips show a Stop using this project button; the skill chip named in Expected is not in the composer code.
steps: Click the + button at the bottom left of the composer.
Under "Add context", click one item, for example Open editors.
Look: a chip appears in the strip above the box with a name and an × button.
Click the × on the chip and look: it disappears.
S13.31.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Add context > Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output or Web page

labels.text: Browse the web for current sources

S13.32.needs: a signed-in account; Browse the web is greyed out when web search is denied
S13.32.note: Connector resources and page sources as chips were not found in this strip; only the web browsing chip is in the composer markup.
steps: Click the + button, then click Browse the web under Tools.
Look: a chip reading "Browse the web for current sources" appears above the composer.
Click the × on that chip (Remove web browsing) and look: the chip goes away.
S13.32.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Tools > Browse the web

S13.33.note: Research, code and office-file tools named in Expected were not found in this menu; only Browse the web and Plan mode appear under Tools, and Plan mode shows as the mode button rather than a chip.
steps: Click the + button and look at the Tools heading.
Click Plan mode.
Look at the mode button at the bottom of the composer (next to the model): it changes to the plan mode label.
Click Browse the web under Tools and look for its chip above the composer.
S13.33.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Tools > Plan mode or Browse the web

S13.35.note: The menu lists text files under Attach workspace files; no media entry appears in the menu, and images come in by paste or drop.
steps: Click the + button.
Look at the menu titled Add context: Attach workspace files, Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output, Web page.
Look under Tools: Browse the web, Set up web search, Plan mode.
Click Attach workspace files and check that a file picker opens.
S13.35.where: AGI Code sidebar > + button (tooltip "Attach or use tools") at the bottom left of the composer

S13.38.needs: a reply that takes a few seconds to generate
S13.38.note: The label reads Steer instead when the Active-turn send setting is set to Steer.
steps: Send a prompt that gives a long reply.
While it is still streaming, type a second message in the box "Describe a task…".
Look: the send button's label reads Queue.
Click it and look: your message appears in the chat with a Queued tag and sends after the reply finishes.
S13.38.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer, while a reply is generating > type in the box > send button labelled Queue

S13.39.needs: a reply that is still streaming
S13.39.note: Edit is refused while the box has text; the message tells you to send or clear the box first.
steps: Queue a message while a reply is streaming (see S13.38).
Look under the queued message for two small icon buttons, Edit and Cancel.
Click Cancel: the queued message is removed and not sent.
Queue another message, clear the box "Describe a task…", click Edit and look: the text goes back into the box.
S13.39.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat > the queued message shows Edit and Cancel buttons under it

S13.40.needs: a reply that is still running
S13.40.note: The package.json description says conflicts fall back to the next-turn queue; I did not verify that fallback.
steps: Open Settings from the gear icon in the AGI Code sidebar.
Find Session behavior and set Active-turn send to Steer current turn.
Start a long reply, then type guidance in the box "Describe a task…" and send it while it runs.
Look: the send button reads Steer, and the message shows a Steered tag while the reply keeps going.
S13.40.where: AGI Code sidebar > gear (Code: Open Settings) > Session behavior > Active-turn send > Steer current turn
